intro: German marks focus with small words placed directly before the element they single out, and with the Vorfeld, the slot before the finite verb. This quiz drills the focus particles a careful writer must choose between: selbst and sogar (even) – interchangeable before a noun phrase and in selbst / sogar wenn, but only sogar can focus a verb, while selbst after a noun means himself (der Minister selbst); nicht einmal (not even); noch before a comparative (noch schwächer); ausgerechnet and gerade (of all days / of all people); genau, eben and gerade (exactly, precisely – gerade weil); erst (not until, only so far, only forty) against nur, bloß, lediglich (merely); allein, schon, bereits (the mere thought); zumindest / wenigstens (at least); erst recht (all the more). One item asks you to front an object for contrast (Den ersten Vorschlag lehne ich ab …). Where two or three particles are equally natural, every one of them is accepted; the English cue tells you which meaning is wanted, and the tips explain where the particles part company.
tips[0].title: even: selbst, sogar, nicht einmal, noch
tips[0].text: Before a noun phrase selbst and sogar are interchangeable: Selbst / Sogar der Chef wusste nichts. Before a verb or a whole predicate only sogar works: Sie hat es sogar angenommen. After the noun, selbst means himself / herself: Der Minister selbst hat es eingeräumt. Negated even is nicht einmal (colloquially nicht mal). With a comparative German says noch: noch schwächer, noch besser (sogar noch for extra weight). Concessive even if: selbst wenn, auch wenn, sogar wenn.
tips[0].trap: Der Chef selbst wusste nichts means the boss himself (in person) knew nothing – not even the boss. The position of selbst changes the meaning.
tips[0].check.why: Before a comparative, English even is noch in German; selbst cannot stand there.
tips[1].title: ausgerechnet, gerade, genau, eben
tips[1].text: ausgerechnet = of all people / things / days, with a note of annoyance or surprise: ausgerechnet heute, ausgerechnet ich. gerade can carry the same meaning (gerade heute, gerade du solltest das wissen) and also means precisely: gerade weil, gerade das. genau and eben = exactly: genau / eben das habe ich gesagt. In the Vorfeld before a demonstrative or a weil-clause, gerade, eben and genau are often all possible.
tips[1].check.why: ausgerechnet means of all days and carries the note of annoyance; erst, schon and nur say something else about time or quantity.
tips[2].title: erst vs nur; allein, schon, erst recht, zumindest
tips[2].text: erst = only in time or sequence (so far / not until / surprisingly early): erst halb acht, erst nach Jahren, erst vierzig. nur, bloß, lediglich = only in quantity (no more than): nur fünf Euro; ganze fünf Euro says the same with irony. allein / schon / bereits der Gedanke = the mere thought. zumindest / wenigstens = at least. erst recht = all the more.
tips[2].trap: Es ist nur drei Uhr is heard in speech, but in careful German the temporal only is erst.
tips[2].check.why: Temporal only (not until) is erst; nur, bloß and lediglich limit a quantity and would mean only tomorrow, on no other day.
tips[2].visual.rows[1].a: Ich habe erst drei Seiten gelesen. (more to come)
tips[2].visual.rows[1].b: Ich habe nur drei Seiten gelesen. (that's all)
tips[3].title: The Vorfeld is the focus slot
tips[3].text: Whatever stands before the finite verb gets attention. Put an object there and it becomes a contrast: Den ersten Vorschlag lehne ich ab, den zweiten nehme ich an. Put a particle plus noun there and the particle’s meaning is in the spotlight: Ausgerechnet ihm passierte das. Neutral sentences begin with the subject or with what links to the previous sentence (theme); new information goes to the end (rheme).
tips[3].check.why: The contrasted object moves into the Vorfeld but stays accusative: ich kenne seinen Bruder → Seinen Bruder kenne ich.
remember[0]: selbst = sogar before a noun phrase; only sogar before a verb; der Minister selbst = himself.
remember[1]: not even = nicht einmal; even + comparative = noch.
remember[2]: Temporal only = erst; quantity only = nur / bloß / lediglich.
remember[3]: Where several particles fit, all are right – the cue fixes the meaning, not the word.
mistakes[0].why: Temporal only is erst; nur limits a quantity.
mistakes[1].why: selbst before the noun = even; after it = himself.
mistakes[2].why: Only sogar can focus a verb; selbst here reads as she herself accepted it.
mistakes[3].why: Before a comparative, even is noch (or sogar noch).
hook: One small word in the right place moves the spotlight: selbst, ausgerechnet, erst and the slot before the verb decide what your sentence stresses.
